discussion_comments.comment_body: Fixed in e8f733f68c. A row's id is now built from the revision of the turn's first set, so it keeps that id all turn. Each new set still gets its own revision. After skipping Review, Wrap up keeps its id, and the desktop's highlight stays on it. Use, Send, Skip and Undo skip name a row by that id. Only refresh still needs the current revision, because its `more` cause names no row. The per-turn revision list was dropped, and a test pins the stable ids.

Fixed in 85ba54c1e8. When a Skip names a row that sits before the cursor (one New set already paged past), the cursor now moves back by one. Only the skipped row leaves the pool, and the rows on screen stay put. A test pins your sequence: New set, then a late Skip for Verify, leaves Review/Wrap up/Next step in view, and Undo skip brings Verify back to the front. I also fuzzed 4,000 random verb sequences offline against "a skip hides only its row, more drops only the last row, Undo skip brings its row into view". The fuzzer finds this bug without the fix and finds nothing with it.

Valid, fixed. A link whose target is a directory already on the current copy chain, or an ancestor of one (`.`, `..`, a sibling that links back), is now skipped and listed in `skippedPaths` instead of being expanded again, and the number of linked-directory expansions is capped (`MAX_LINK_EXPANSIONS`). Covered by "skips links that loop back into a directory being copied": twenty links to `.` plus one to `..` finish in well under a second with only the real content copied.
